target_customer: Developers of voice agents, meeting notetakers and captioning products, plus deaf and hard-of-hearing consumers via captioning glasses
problem: Speech models degrade with noise, overlapping speakers and distant audio; hard-of-hearing people lack affordable live captioning in person.
business_model: Usage-based speech API (for example $0.18 per audio hour for async) plus captioning glasses hardware and subscription
product_category: Voice AI speech-to-text and AR captioning glasses

founders.name: Madhav Lavakare
previous_startups: TranscribeGlass (earlier name of the same project)
founders.background_notes: Began prototype at age 16 in 2017 after a hard-of-hearing classmate struggled; Yale alumni magazine.

founders.name: Nirbhay Narang
prior_employers: First engineer at early-stage YC voice AI startups
education: Cornell, computer science, summa cum laude
founders.background_notes: 8VC and Kessler Fellowships per YC page.

competitors.name: XRAI Glass
competitors.what: AR captioning glasses (AR One, later AR2)

technical_complexity.rationale: Robust diarization and speaker ID in noisy far-field audio is hard ML, plus custom glasses hardware built on Vuzix; claims top ranks on a public diarization benchmark (company stated).

defensibility.rationale: Benchmark leadership and models are a moat only while they stay ahead of AssemblyAI, Deepgram, OpenAI and others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: OpenAI launched new voice models in May 2026 (press), raising pressure on speech API startups; no copying of the glasses wedge found.

market_need_then: The Yale alumni magazine reports a July 2023 TikTok with a claimed 75 million views and a waitlist over 10,000, showing demand for captioning glasses; the first pair shipped in February 2025.

branding.name_origin: Renamed from TranscribeGlass to AirCaps in 2025 to expand beyond captions into translation and meeting summaries, per the company LinkedIn post as summarized in search results.
branding.domain_note: Company site is aircaps.ai; LinkedIn handle is tryaircaps.

identity.visual_style: Black-frame captioning glasses with floating text display
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and technical; AI learned to talk, we are teaching it to listen

branding.brand_signature: Live captions floating in the lens, popularized by a viral 2023 TikTok

rebrands.why: Broaden from captions to translation and meeting notes (company LinkedIn per search summary)

branding.community_and_virality: Viral TikTok in July 2023 with a claimed 75 million views and a 10,000 person waitlist (Yale alumni magazine); coverage in Wired and PC Gamer.

brand_strength.rationale: The predecessor brand earned real virality and press, but the rename to AirCaps resets recognition and the new API pivot targets developers.

pivots.to: AirCaps: voice AI models and speech API alongside the glasses
pivots.why: Expansion beyond captions into translation, meeting notes and developer speech models per company announcement.

outcome_analysis: AirCaps grew out of a Yale student's captioning glasses project that went viral in 2023, shipped its first glasses in early 2025 and joined YC in Fall 2025 with a rebrand and a speech API. It claims leading diarization benchmark results. Funding is unclear, with conflicting small figures, and it faces large voice AI incumbents. It is active and unexited.
notes: Funding sources conflict: VCBacked and FundedIQ show a 500K pre-seed (Dec 2025), CB Insights a seed dated June 2026, Caplight a seed dated Sept 2025 totaling 1M, another source about 130K. All aggregators, none verified, so no rounds recorded. YC page says founded 2024 and Yale article describes a 2017 prototype and 2023 virality. Competitor entries come from 2026 sources, not founding-date sources. Wired review only found on a mirror domain.
